briefdescription.para: Initializes a specific XCanFd instance/driver.

detaileddescription.para: This function should only be used when no Virtual Memory support is needed.

This initialization entails:
Search for device configuration given the device ID.
Initialize Base Address field of the XCanFd structure using the device address in the found device configuration.
Populate all other data fields in the XCanFd structure.
Reset the device.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Pointer to XCanFd_Config instance.
Base address of CANFD.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if initialization was successful.
XST_DEVICE_NOT_FOUND if device configuration information was not found for a device with the supplied device ID.

briefdescription.para: Returns enabled acceptance filters.

detaileddescription.para: Use XCANFD_AFR_UAF*_MASK defined in xcanfd_hw.h to interpret the returned value. If no acceptance filters are enabled then all received frames are stored in the RX FIFO.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.

simplesect.para: The value stored in Acceptance Filter Register.

Acceptance Filter Register is an optional register in Xilinx CAN device. If it is NOT existing in the device, this function should NOT be used. Calling this function in this case causes an assertion failure.

briefdescription.para: Returns the current operation mode of the CAN device.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.

simplesect.para:
- XCANFD_MODE_CONFIG if the device is in Configuration Mode.
XCANFD_MODE_SLEEP if the device is in Sleep Mode.

listitem.para: XCANFD_MODE_NORMAL if the device is in Normal Mode.
XCANFD_MODE_LOOPBACK if the device is in Loop Back Mode.
XCANFD_MODE_SNOOP if the device is in Snoop Mode.
XCANFD_MODE_BR if the device is in Bus-Off recovery Mode.
XCANFD_MODE_PEE if the device is in Protocol Exception Event mode.

briefdescription.para: Enters the specified CAN operation mode.

detaileddescription.para: Allows the CAN device to enter one of the following operation modes:

listitem.para: Configuration Mode: Pass in parameter XCANFD_MODE_CONFIG
Sleep Mode: Pass in parameter XCANFD_MODE_SLEEP
Normal Mode: Pass in parameter XCANFD_MODE_NORMAL
Loop Back Mode: Pass in parameter XCANFD_MODE_LOOPBACK
Snoop Mode: Pass in Parameter XCANFD_MODE_SNOOP
Auto Bus-Off Recovery Mode: Pass in Parameter XCANFD_MODE_ABR
Start Bus-Off Recovery Mode: Pass in Parameter XCANFD_MODE_SBR
Protocol Exception Event Mode: Pass in Parameter XCANFD_MODE_PEE
Disable AutoRetransmission Mode: Pass in Parameter XCANFD_MODE_DAR

detaileddescription.para: Read xcanfd.h and device specification for detailed description of each operation mode.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Specifies which operation mode to enter. Valid value is any of XCANFD_MODE_* defined in xcanfd.h. Note that no multiple modes could be entered at the same time.

simplesect.para: This function does NOT ensure CAN device enters the specified operation mode before returns the control to the caller. The caller is responsible for checking current operation mode using XCanFd_GetMode().

briefdescription.para: Sends a CAN/CANFD Frame.

detaileddescription.para: Checks whether a free buffer is available. If a free buffer exists, the supplied data is written into it. Otherwise returns an error code immediately. Does not wait for the given frame to be sent to the CAN bus.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer containing the CAN frame to be sent.
Buffer where the supplied data has been written and it is updated by driver.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if TX FIFO was not full and the given frame was written into the FIFO.
XST_FIFO_NO_ROOM if there is no room in the TX FIFO for the given frame.

briefdescription.para: Writes data into a specific TX buffer.

detaileddescription.para: There are 32 TX buffers. Data can be added to each buffer using this function. This function does not transmit the data; it only adds data to the buffers.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer containing the CAN frame to be sent.
Buffer Number where the data has been written and is given back to user.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if TX FIFO was not full and the given frame was written into the FIFO.
XST_FIFO_NO_ROOM if there is no room in the TX FIFO for the given frame.

briefdescription.para: Receives a CAN/CAN FD Frame in sequential mode.

detaileddescription.para: Checks the FSR Register. The FL bits indicate the number of packets received. If FL is non-zero, reads the packet and stores it to the supplied buffer.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer where the CAN/CAN FD frame is to be written.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if RX FIFO was not empty and a frame was read from RX FIFO successfully and written into the given buffer.
XST_NO_DATA if there is no frame to be received from the FIFO.

The CANFD has two design modes. ->Sequential Mode - Core writes data sequentially to RxBuffers. ->MailBox Mode - Core writes data to RxBuffers when a ID Match happened. This routine distinguishes receive checking as per the frame availability from either Fifo 0 or Fifo 1.

briefdescription.para: Receives CAN/CAN FD TX Events in sequential mode.

detaileddescription.para: Checks the FSR Register. The FL bits indicate the number of TX Event packets received. If FL is non-zero, reads the packet and stores it to the supplied buffer.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer where the CAN/CAN FD frame Event is to be written.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if TXE FIFO was not empty and a frame was read from TX FIFO successfully and written into the given buffer.
XST_NO_DATA if there is no frame to be received from the TXE FIFO.

This CANFD has two design modes. ->Sequential Mode - Core writes data sequentially to RxBuffers. ->MailBox Mode - Core writes data to RxBuffers when a ID Match happened. This routine is useful for Both the Modes. This API is meant to be used with IP with CanFD 2.0 spec support only.

briefdescription.para: Receives a CAN Frame in Mailbox Mode.

detaileddescription.para: Reads the Rx Last Buffer Index from the ISR Register. This indicates which buffer contains data. Then reads and updates the data to the supplied buffer.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer where the CAN frame is to be received.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if RX FIFO was not empty and a frame was read from RX FIFO successfully and written into the given buffer.
XST_NO_DATA if there is no frame to be received from the FIFO.

This CANFD has two design modes. ->Sequential Mode - Core writes data sequentially to RxBuffers. ->MailBox Mode - Core writes data to RxBuffers when a ID match happened. This routine is useful for MailBox Mode.

briefdescription.para: Sets an RxBuffer to Active State.

detaileddescription.para: In Mailbox Mode configuration each buffer can be set to receive with a specific Id and Mask. The buffer must first be activated before comparison. Maximum number of RxBuffers depends on Design. Range 48, 32, 16.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Receive Buffer Number that defines which Buffer to configure. Value ranges from 0 - 48.

simplesect.para: - XST_SUCCESS if the values were set successfully.

simplesect.para: - XST_SUCCESS if the values were set successfully.

briefdescription.para: Sets an RxBuffer to Inactive State.

detaileddescription.para: If a buffer is changed to Inactive state, Rx packets are not stored into that buffer, even if the Id is matched.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Receive Buffer Number that defines which Buffer to configure. Value ranges from 0 - 48.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if the values were set successfully.
XST_FAILURE if the given filter was not disabled, or the CAN device was not ready to accept writes to AFMR and AFIR.

briefdescription.para: Cancels a CAN/CAN FD Frame transmission request.

detaileddescription.para: Checks the TRR Bit based on BufferNumber. If the TRR Bit is set, cancels the buffer transmission.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Which Buffer to cancel out of 32 Buffers.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if cancellation was successful.
XST_FAILURE if the buffer has no pending transmission.

This function first checks whether the TRR bit is set.
If it is set, the function checks the corresponding TCR bit.
If the TCR bit is set, the function waits until cancellation is performed.
If the TCR bit is not set, the function sets it and waits until the core clears it.
If the TRR bit is not set, the function does nothing.

briefdescription.para: Enables the acceptance filters.

detaileddescription.para: Up to 32 filters can be enabled.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.

Specifies which filters to enable. Use any XCANFD_AFR_UAF*_MASK to enable one filter, and combine multiple XCANFD_AFR_UAF*_MASK values with a bitwise OR to enable multiple filters. Any filter not specified in this parameter keeps its previous enable or disable setting.

simplesect.para: In Sequential Mode, enable these filters to receive data. To filter by Id match, set the Id value in the AFR Id register.

briefdescription.para: Disables the acceptance filters.

detaileddescription.para: 32 filters can be disabled.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.

Specifies which filters to disable. Use any XCANFD_AFR_UAF*_MASK to disable one filter, and combine multiple XCANFD_AFR_UAF*_MASK values with a bitwise OR to disable multiple filters. Any filter not specified in this parameter keeps its previous enable or disable setting. If all acceptance filters are disabled then all received frames are stored in the RX FIFO.

briefdescription.para: Sets values for the Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Registers.

detaileddescription.para: Sets values to the Acceptance Filter Mask Register (AFMR) and Acceptance Filter ID Register (AFIR) for the specified Acceptance Filter. Use XCANFD_IDR_* defined in xcanfd_hw.h to create the values to set the filter. Read xcanfd.h and device specification for details.

This function should be called only after:
The given filter is disabled by calling XCanFd_AcceptFilterDisable().
And the CAN device is ready to accept writes to AFMR and AFIR, that is, XCanFd_IsAcceptFilterBusy() returns FALSE.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Defines which Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Register to set. Use any single XCANFD_AFR_UAF*_MASK value. Ranges from 1 - 32.
Value to write to the chosen Acceptance Filter Mask Register.
Value to write to the chosen Acceptance Filter ID Register.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if the values were set successfully.
XST_FAILURE if the given filter was not disabled, or the CAN device was not ready to accept writes to AFMR and AFIR.
Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Registers are optional registers in Xilinx XCanFd device. If they are not configured then the device receives data with any ID.

briefdescription.para: Reads the Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Register values.

detaileddescription.para: Reads the values of the Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Register for the specified Acceptance Filter. Use XCANFD_IDR_* defined in xcanfd_hw.h to interpret the values. Read xcanfd.h and device specification for details.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Defines which Acceptance Filter Mask Register to get Mask and ID from. Use any single XCANFD_FILTER_* value.
Mask value read from the chosen Acceptance Filter Mask Register after this function returns.
ID value read from the chosen Acceptance Filter ID Register after this function returns.

simplesect.para: Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Registers are optional registers in Xilinx CAN device. If they are NOT existing in the device, this function should NOT be used. Calling this function in this case causes an assertion failure.
